Google is sending higher quality traffic than ChatGPT in the last 60 days.

In the past 18 months, ChatGPT's quality is 2% better, but that continues to decline.

The narrative that LLMs are better in a generalized view is becoming less true than ever.

What’s likely the cause of the sentiment that it drives better traffic than Google?

First, the outliers are the loudest voices. There are websites driving 5% of their traffic from ChatGPT, and these are likely also where engagement is highest.

But that’s not a B2C website selling holiday cards. 

There, where rich, multi-modal experiences are more needed, the relative ChatGPT experience is actually less than ideal.

Additionally, ChatGPT has been making some model changes in the past few months. Some would say for the better, some would say for the worse. 

This may be reflected partially in swings in engagement data across our sample.

Finally, ChatGPT is also experiencing seasonality swings, with their first MOM declines in referral traffic in July and August. 

It’s possible this is a change in who uses the service as well, driving a mild downtick in engagement.

One of the clearest trends emerging from ChatGPT coming on the scene: divergence. 

There is risk if you overcorrect your point of view towards LLMs when your audience is not yet there. 

Yes, it’s important to be future thinking, but we can’t accept generalized LinkedIn voices as equivalent for every audience. 

You can find our full ChatGPT / Google engagement rate study of 304 sites in the Learn dropdown on our website. | 20 comments on LinkedIn
